page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c2.medium is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the ecs.c2 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include integrated local storage or bundled GPU hardware, requiring external block storage for operating system and application data.

With a dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides predictable compute performance for workloads that require sustained processor utilization without virtualization-induced throttling. The 1:1 ratio of vCPUs to memory makes this instance highly specialized for compute-bound tasks where memory footprint requirements are minimal. Qualitatively, this hardware profile offers cost efficiency for processing-heavy workloads by avoiding the added expense of unneeded memory capacity, though the lack of local storage and bundled public IPv4 addresses requires careful architectural planning for external dependencies.

The ecs.c2.medium is designed for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand large memory allocations or local storage. Suitable use cases include batch processing, distributed analytics nodes, high-performance computing (HPC) tasks, and CPU-bound microservices.
